4:1.sourceText: Λαλούντων δὲ αὐτῶν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν, ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς οἱ ἱερεῖς καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι,
4:1.targetText: And as they are speaking to the people, there came to them the priests, and the magistrate of the temple, and the Sadducees—

groups.note: The actual genitive speaking participle with its personal subject supplies the temporal as-they-are-speaking clause; as makes that circumstantial construction explicit without a separate Greek time conjunction.

4:2.sourceText: διαπονούμενοι διὰ τὸ διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς τὸν λαὸν καὶ καταγγέλλειν ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὴν ἀνάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
4:2.targetText: being grieved because of their teaching the people, and preaching in Jesus the resurrection out of the dead—

groups.note: Actual αὐτούς is the accusative subject of the teaching/preaching infinitives. English their nominalizes that same subject as the possessor of teaching; the source personal identity is not relabeled as genitive.

unmappedSource.reason: The articular-infinitive article, the article with Jesus, and the repeated resurrection modifier article are not separately expressed in English.

4:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐπέβαλον αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ἔθεντο εἰς τήρησιν εἰς τὴν αὔριον· ἦν γὰρ ἑσπέρα ἤδη.
4:3.targetText: and they laid hands on them, and put them in custody until the next day, for it was evening already;

groups.note: The one actual dative personal object names the same people in the immediate laying-hands-on / putting-in-custody coordination. English states on them and then them, retaining one written personal identity rather than inventing another pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with laid hands.

4:4.sourceText: πολλοὶ δὲ τῶν ἀκουσάντων τὸν λόγον ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ ἐγενήθη ἀριθμὸς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ὡς χιλιάδες πέντε.
4:4.targetText: and many of those hearing the word believed, and the number of the men became, as it were, five thousand.

4:5.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον συναχθῆναι αὐτῶν τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ,
4:5.targetText: And it came to pass the next day, there were gathered together of them the rulers, and elders, and scribes, to Jerusalem,

groups.note: The actual ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον supplies the next-day time expression. English has no independent on/at word, so the time constituent is retained together.
Actual συναχθῆναι is an aorist passive infinitive under came to pass; English makes it the finite there-were-gathered-together clause. The printed infinitive remains explicit.
Actual ἐν introduces Jerusalem as the gathering location. LSV prints directional to Jerusalem; the original ἐν form remains rather than being overwritten by εἰς.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately repeated with elders and scribes in the English list.

4:6.sourceText: καὶ Ἄννας ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ Καϊάφας καὶ Ἰωάνης καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος καὶ ὅσοι ἦσαν ἐκ γένους ἀρχιερατικοῦ,
4:6.targetText: and Annas the chief priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the family of the chief priest,

groups.note: Actual ἀρχιερατικοῦ is the high-priestly adjective qualifying family. English recasts that adjectival relation as of the chief priest; no additional chief-priest noun is printed at this point.

4:7.sourceText: καὶ στήσαντες αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ μέσῳ ἐπυνθάνοντο Ἐν ποίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ ἐν ποίῳ ὀνόματι ἐποιήσατε τοῦτο ὑμεῖς;
4:7.targetText: and having set them in the midst, they were inquiring, “In what power, or in what name did you do this?”

4:8.sourceText: τότε Πέτρος πλησθεὶς Πνεύματος Ἁγίου εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ πρεσβύτεροι,
4:8.targetText: Then Peter, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: “Rulers of the people, and elders of Israel,

groups.note: Actual genitive Spirit supplies the filling content, rendered with the Spirit; no separate Greek with preposition is printed.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the elders-of-Israel qualifier, corroborated by TR Ἰσραήλ. Pinned N1904 has elders without that place-name qualifier.

4:9.sourceText: εἰ ἡμεῖς σήμερον ἀνακρινόμεθα ἐπὶ εὐεργεσίᾳ ἀνθρώπου ἀσθενοῦς, ἐν τίνι οὗτος σέσωσται,
4:9.targetText: if we are examined today concerning the good deed to the ailing man, by whom he has been saved,

groups.note: The actual genitive man noun qualifies the good deed as its recipient/object. English expresses that objective relation as to the ... man without a separately printed Greek to preposition.
Actual οὗτος is the demonstrative this one, rendered he for the same nearby man; its demonstrative source form remains available.

4:10.sourceText: γνωστὸν ἔστω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν καὶ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραὴλ, ὅτι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου, ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε, ὃν ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐν τούτῳ οὗτος παρέστηκεν ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ὑγιής.
4:10.targetText: be it known to all of you, and to all the people of Israel, that in the Name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised out of the dead, in Him has this one stood by before you whole.

groups.note: Actual ὑμῖν is dative to you with the dative all. English to all of you recasts the same recipients as an of-you complement, without a source genitive form or separate of preposition.
Actual τούτῳ is the dative demonstrative this one/this, rendered Him in the preceding in phrase. The printed demonstrative is retained rather than relabeled as αὐτῷ.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

4:11.sourceText: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ λίθος ὁ ἐξουθενηθεὶς ὑφ’ ὑμῶν τῶν οἰκοδόμων, ὁ γενόμενος εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας.
4:11.targetText: This is the stone that was set at nothing by you—the builders, that became head of a corner;

groups.note: Actual εἰς κεφαλήν is the become-to/as-head result construction. English became head omits an independent to/as word, so the real preposition/head constituent is retained together.

4:12.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ ἡ σωτηρία· οὐδὲ γὰρ ὄνομά ἐστιν ἕτερον ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸ δεδομένον ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἐν ᾧ δεῖ σωθῆναι ἡμᾶς.
4:12.targetText: and there is not salvation in any other, for there is no other name under Heaven that has been given among men, in which it is required of us to be saved.”

groups.note: Actual οὐδέ is the negative connector not-even/nor. English renders the second negative proposition with no other name, without a separate even/nor word.
Actual ἡμᾶς is the accusative personal subject of the being-saved infinitive. English of us recasts that subject after required; no source genitive form or of preposition is substituted.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with salvation and Heaven.

4:13.sourceText: Θεωροῦντες δὲ τὴν τοῦ Πέτρου παρρησίαν καὶ Ἰωάνου, καὶ καταλαβόμενοι ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ἀγράμματοί εἰσιν καὶ ἰδιῶται, ἐθαύμαζον, ἐπεγίνωσκόν τε αὐτοὺς ὅτι σὺν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἦσαν,
4:13.targetText: And beholding the openness of Peter and John, and having perceived that they are illiterate men and commoners, they were wondering—they were also taking knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus—

groups.note: Actual αὐτούς is the accusative recognition object, rendered of them as part of taking knowledge of them; no genitive Greek pronoun or separate of preposition is printed.
Actual ἦσαν is imperfect they were. English had been uses past-perfect wording for this same being-with predicate; the original imperfect remains.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with Jesus.

4:14.sourceText: τόν τε ἄνθρωπον βλέποντες σὺν αὐτοῖς ἑστῶτα τὸν τεθεραπευμένον, οὐδὲν εἶχον ἀντειπεῖν.
4:14.targetText: and seeing the man standing with them who has been healed, they had nothing to say against [it],

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed object of saying against; no object pronoun is printed in this verse.

4:15.sourceText: κελεύσαντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔξω τοῦ συνεδρίου ἀπελθεῖν, συνέβαλλον πρὸς ἀλλήλους
4:15.targetText: and having commanded them to go away out of the Sanhedrin, they took counsel with one another,

groups.note: Actual συνέδριον names the council/council assembly, conventionally rendered Sanhedrin; the printed noun remains the source.

4:16.sourceText: λέγοντες Τί ποιήσωμεν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις; ὅτι μὲν γὰρ γνωστὸν σημεῖον γέγονεν δι’ αὐτῶν, πᾶσιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἱερουσαλὴμ φανερόν, καὶ οὐ δυνάμεθα ἀρνεῖσθαι·
4:16.targetText: saying, “What will we do to these men? Because that, indeed, a notable sign has been done through them [is] apparent to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, and we are not able to deny [it];

groups.note: Actual ποιήσωμεν is the deliberative aorist subjunctive do, rendered will we do in the question rather than a Greek future indicative.
The actual dative article/men constituent supplies the affected people to these men; to belongs to this case-governed construction, not an independently printed Greek preposition.
English [it] after deny resumes the immediately stated sign/its occurrence. The same actual sign noun supplies that local event reference; no independent original object pronoun is printed.
Actual γέγονεν is perfect become/happen, rendered has been done with sign; no separate source doing verb is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula with apparent; the Greek predicate adjective has no separate printed be word.

4:17.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ἵνα μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖον διανεμηθῇ εἰς τὸν λαόν, ἀπειλησώμεθα αὐτοῖς μηκέτι λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ μηδενὶ ἀνθρώπων.
4:17.targetText: but that it may spread no further toward the people, let us strictly threaten them to no longer speak in this Name to any man.”

groups.note: Actual μηδενὶ ἀνθρώπων is the negative nobody-of-people recipient constituent. LSV expresses it as to any man under the preceding no-longer prohibition; the actual negative force remains in that construction, not an invented positive indefinite source.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this Name.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds the emphatic threatening expression, corroborated by the TR ἀπειλῇ noun alongside threaten. Pinned N1904 has the threatening verb without that separate intensifier noun.

4:18.sourceText: καὶ καλέσαντες αὐτοὺς παρήγγειλαν καθόλου μὴ φθέγγεσθαι μηδὲ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
4:18.targetText: And having called them, they charged them not to speak at all, nor to teach, in the Name of Jesus,

groups.note: The one printed personal object identifies the same people in the immediate called/charged coordination. English repeats them for both predicates without a second written source pronoun.

4:19.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάνης ἀποκριθέντες εἶπον πρὸς αὐτούς Εἰ δίκαιόν ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὑμῶν ἀκούειν μᾶλλον ἢ τοῦ Θεοῦ, κρίνατε·
4:19.targetText: and Peter and John answering to them said, “Whether it is righteous before God to listen to you rather than to God, judge;

groups.note: Actual genitive ὑμῶν is the hearing/listening object, rendered to you with listen; no separate Greek to preposition is printed here.
The actual genitive article/God constituent is the coordinated listening object, rendered to God. The hearing-object case and real noun remain one source construction.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Peter and the first God designation.

4:20.sourceText: οὐ δυνάμεθα γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἃ εἴδαμεν καὶ ἠκούσαμεν μὴ λαλεῖν.
4:20.targetText: for we cannot but speak what we saw and heard.”

groups.note: Actual μή negates speak after the preceding cannot: the Greek construction is cannot not speak. English renders that double-negative necessity idiom as cannot but speak; this but is not a printed ἀλλά conjunction.

4:21.sourceText: οἱ δὲ προσαπειλησάμενοι ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς, μηδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τὸ πῶς κολάσωνται αὐτούς, διὰ τὸν λαόν, ὅτι πάντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεὸν ἐπὶ τῷ γεγονότι·
4:21.targetText: And they having further threatened [them], let them go, finding no way how they may punish them, because of the people, because all were glorifying God for that which has been done,

groups.note: The actual personal object of let-go identifies the same people in the immediately preceding further-threatening participle. English repeats [them] and them for those coordinated local acts, retaining one real object identity.
Actual γεγονότι is the perfect become/happen participle, rendered has been done in the nominal event phrase; no separate ποιέω doing lemma is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The article nominalizing the how/punish deliberation is not separately expressed in English.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

4:22.sourceText: ἐτῶν γὰρ ἦν πλειόνων τεσσεράκοντα ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐφ’ ὃν γεγόνει τὸ σημεῖον τοῦτο τῆς ἰάσεως.
4:22.targetText: for above forty years of age was the man on whom had been done this sign of the healing.

groups.note: Actual γεγόνει is pluperfect become/happen, rendered had been done with the healing sign; the actual become/happen head remains.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this sign.

4:23.sourceText: Ἀπολυθέντες δὲ ἦλθον πρὸς τοὺς ἰδίους καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ὅσα πρὸς αὐτοὺς οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι εἶπαν.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with their own friends.

4:24.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἦραν φωνὴν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ εἶπαν Δέσποτα, σὺ ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς,
4:24.targetText: and they having heard, lifted up the voice to God with one accord and said, “LORD, You [are] God, who made the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all that [are] in them,

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the explicit God predication, corroborated by the TR ὁ Θεός wording. Pinned N1904 has You followed directly by the who-made participial construction, without a second God noun or a be verb here.
English supplies a copula in all that are in them; there is no separate Greek be word in this location modifier.

4:25.sourceText: ὁ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν διὰ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου στόματος Δαυεὶδ παιδός σου εἰπών Ἵνα τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν κενά;
4:25.targetText: who, through the mouth of Your servant David, said, Why did nations rage, and peoples meditate vain things?

groups.note: The actual genitive servant noun gives the mouth-of-Your-servant-David relation, rendered of ... servant without a separate Greek of preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 includes the of-our-father constituent. LSV follows the shorter TR wording without that father noun, possessive, or article.

4:26.sourceText: παρέστησαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ.
4:26.targetText: The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the LORD and against His Christ;

groups.note: Actual ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό supplies the together expression in the gathering clause; the real three-word idiom is kept instead of inventing a separate together adverb.

groups.note: The one actual σου qualifies hand and its coordinated counsel. English repeats Your on each member; both local possessive renderings retain one written personal identity.

4:29.sourceText: καὶ τὰ νῦν, Κύριε, ἔπιδε ἐπὶ τὰς ἀπειλὰς αὐτῶν, καὶ δὸς τοῖς δούλοις σου μετὰ παρρησίας πάσης λαλεῖν τὸν λόγον σου,
4:29.targetText: And now, LORD, look on their threatenings, and grant to Your servants to speak Your word with all freedom,

groups.note: The actual dative article/servants constituent supplies the grant recipients to Your servants; no independent Greek to preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed in now, their threatenings, and Your word.

4:30.sourceText: ἐν τῷ τὴν χεῖρά ἐκτείνειν σε εἰς ἴασιν καὶ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ ἁγίου Παιδός σου Ἰησοῦ.
4:30.targetText: in the stretching forth of Your hand, for healing, and signs, and wonders, to come to pass through the Name of Your holy child Jesus.”

groups.note: The actual hand noun is the object of stretching forth. English of ... hand expresses that same object as the complement of nominal stretching forth; no independent Greek of preposition is printed.

The actual genitive child noun gives the Name-of-Your-child relation, rendered of ... child without a separately printed Greek of preposition.

4:31.sourceText: καὶ δεηθέντων αὐτῶν ἐσαλεύθη ὁ τόπος ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν συνηγμένοι, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ἅπαντες τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος, καὶ ἐλάλουν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ μετὰ παρρησίας.
4:31.targetText: And they having prayed, the place was shaken in which they were gathered together, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and were speaking the word of God with freedom,

groups.note: The actual genitive article/Spirit constituent carries the filling content. Its case-and-definiteness wording with the is retained; the real Holy and Spirit words remain separately selectable.

4:32.sourceText: Τοῦ δὲ πλήθους τῶν πιστευσάντων ἦν καρδία καὶ ψυχὴ μία, καὶ οὐδὲ εἷς τι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ ἔλεγεν ἴδιον εἶναι, ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτοῖς πάντα κοινά.

4:33.sourceText: καὶ δυνάμει μεγάλῃ ἀπεδίδουν τὸ μαρτύριον οἱ ἀπόστολοι τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως, χάρις τε μεγάλη ἦν ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς.
4:33.targetText: And with great power the apostles were giving the testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, great grace was also on them all,

The actual genitive article/resurrection construction identifies the testimony’s subject. English recasts that relation as testimony to the resurrection; no Greek to preposition is printed here.

4:34.sourceText: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐνδεής τις ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς· ὅσοι γὰρ κτήτορες χωρίων ἢ οἰκιῶν ὑπῆρχον, πωλοῦντες ἔφερον τὰς τιμὰς τῶν πιπρασκομένων
4:34.targetText: for there was not anyone among them who lacked, for as many as were possessors of fields, or houses, selling [them], were bringing the prices of the thing sold,
